plain: In 1947 a pilot named Kenneth Arnold reported a group of strange craft racing through the sky in the Pacific Northwest, and his sighting is said to have started the modern UFO era. A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch says Arnold was searching for a downed cargo plane near Mount Rainier, two months before the reported crash at Roswell, New Mexico. A physicist named John Brandenburg adds that soon afterward such craft were being seen all over the country. The author Peter Levenda instead places the flight in the Rockies and stresses the craft's impossible speeds. A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs, describes about half a dozen chevrons moving freely and links them to the phrase "flying saucers"; Jesse Michels says the objects were really crescents and that the word "saucer" came from Arnold's description.
